# Guix dhcpcd can replace osctld-managed resolvers

## Symptom

A Guix container has its expected routed address and default route, but name
resolution fails. `/etc/resolv.conf` contains only:

```text
# Generated by dhcpcd
# /etc/resolv.conf.head can replace this line
# /etc/resolv.conf.tail can replace this line
```

This was reproduced by the managed Guix KB runtime against image `20260819`.
`osctl ct set dns-resolver ... 10.0.2.3` succeeded before startup.

## Cause and fix

The all-interface Guix `dhcpcd-service-type` invokes its `resolv.conf` hook
after osctld has supplied the resolver file. With no DHCP lease providing name
servers, the hook replaces the file with an empty generated configuration.

Configure the service with:

```scheme
(dhcpcd-configuration
  (no-hook '("resolv.conf")))
```

This keeps DHCP interface discovery and the `networking` Shepherd provision,
while leaving resolver ownership with osctld. Guix must also run the shared
`image-scripts/tests/dns_resolver.sh` test; do not exempt it from the delayed
post-start resolver check.

## Verification

The local diagnostic confirmed the configured address and routes alongside the
empty dhcpcd-generated resolver file. Guix 1.5 loaded the corrected module and
reported exactly one dhcpcd service whose `no-hook` value is
`("resolv.conf")`. The Guix-only workflow built the corrected candidate from
known-good `guix/20260613`; its full image runtime suite passed, including the
now-enabled resolver test. Publication and a fresh self-hosted build from
corrected `guix:latest` remain required before removing the temporary recovery
pin.

Related initiative: `work/2026-08-17-image-build-failures/`.
